question: Assume today is 2026-09-14. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of visitor arrivals to Hong Kong in September 2026, as it will be first reported (provisional figure) in the Hong Kong Tourism Board's monthly visitor arrivals press release.

target.what: Total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong (all source markets, all trip purposes, including same-day and overnight visitors) during the calendar month of September 2026, as the provisional figure first published by the Hong Kong Tourism Board in its monthly visitor arrivals press release
target.publisher: Hong Kong Tourism Board (HKTB), monthly visitor arrivals statistics / press release
target.cadence: monthly, provisional figure released roughly 3-5 weeks after month end
target.caveats: Counts are person-trips (arrivals), not unique individuals; a visitor crossing the border multiple times in the month may be counted multiple times. Coverage is all source markets and includes both overnight and same-day (cross-boundary) visitors, mainly from Mainland China. Working interpretation:

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 arrivals = most recent reported monthly arrivals (e.g. July/August 2026) scaled by the historical September-to-summer seasonal ratio and by the year-on-year growth trend. Own history gives both the level and the seasonal shape.
candidates.data_to_find: HKTB monthly total visitor arrivals for each month of 2023, 2024, 2025 and any 2026 months published before 2026-09-14 (Jan-Aug 2026), plus the September values for 2023, 2024, 2025 to derive the September seasonal factor and recent YoY growth rate.
search_hints: HKTB monthly visitor arrivals statistics 2025 September

candidates.hypothesis: HKTB arrivals are derived from Immigration Department arrival records; monthly or daily passenger throughput at land, sea and air control points (especially Mainland visitors via Lo Wu/Lok Ma Chau/High Speed Rail) tracks total arrivals with a stable coverage ratio.
candidates.data_to_find: Immigration Department monthly arrival passenger counts by control point and by visitor vs resident for 2025 and Jan-Aug 2026; daily arrival figures for early September 2026 if published before cutoff; the ratio of HKTB visitor arrivals to total non-resident arrivals.
search_hints: Immigration Department Hong Kong passenger traffic statistics monthly 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Mainland visitors are ~75-80% of total arrivals; estimating Mainland September 2026 arrivals (from mainland outbound travel data, Greater Bay Area travel patterns, or HKTB Mainland figures) and dividing by the Mainland share gives the total.
candidates.data_to_find: HKTB Mainland vs non-Mainland visitor arrivals monthly 2025 and 2026 to date; China outbound travel / Golden Week and Mid-Autumn holiday timing for 2026; any mainland travel-platform data on Hong Kong bookings for September 2026.

candidates.data_to_find: Hong Kong hotel occupancy and room-nights sold for 2025 and 2026 to date; airport passenger arrivals and HSR West Kowloon inbound passenger counts; September 2026 forward bookings or schedule capacity; overnight share of total arrivals.

assessment.note: Same HKTB September 2025 release: p1 is the level and p2 the YoY change; internally consistent (3.29m, +8%). Both are the same underlying measurement, not independent.
September 2025 total decomposes into Mainland (p5) + non-Mainland (p7); the parts sum to the total, confirming internal consistency of the same release.
Mainland September 2025 level and its YoY change from the same release.
Non-Mainland sub-segments (short-haul, long-haul, new markets) are nested within the non-Mainland total; overlapping coverage, same source.
Cumulative Jan-Sep 2025 totals and their components from the same release; consistent with the monthly figures.

p16 (approx 23m in first five months of 2026) implies a 2026 run-rate well above 2025; consistent with continued growth from the 2025 base in p1/p3. Different period and source (govt speech vs HKTB release), so only directional corroboration.

assumptions.name: September-to-August seasonal ratio
assumptions.rationale: September is typically slightly below August in HK arrivals (post-summer, pre-Golden Week); historical Sep/Aug ratios cluster near 0.9-0.95. Used to convert an August 2026 level to September.
assumptions.applies_when: An August 2026 monthly level is available and September is expected to follow the normal seasonal pattern without major typhoon disruption.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual September 2026 event (typhoon, policy change) or a Sep/Aug ratio outside 0.85-1.0 in recent years.

assumptions.name: 2026 YoY growth factor for September vs September 2025
assumptions.rationale: Jan-May 2026 arrivals (~23m, p16) imply strong double-digit growth over 2025; September 2025 was +8% YoY. A 2026 growth factor of ~1.12 is consistent with the 2026 run-rate, tempered toward the 2025 growth rate.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 growth resembles the 2026 year-to-date trend rather than reverting to the 2025 rate.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that 2026 growth decelerated sharply or that September 2026 had a major disruption.

assessment.note: p1 is the September 2025 total level and p2 is its YoY growth; both come from the same HKTB release, so they are internally consistent but not independent. p2 implies a September 2024 base of about 3.05m, consistent with the 2025 recovery trend.
p5 (Mainland) + p7 (non-Mainland) sum to p1 (total), confirming the segment split is exhaustive for September 2025. Same source/release, so this is a definitional check, not independent confirmation.

Segment YoY growth rates (Mainland +7%, non-Mainland +9%, short-haul +9%, long-haul +14%, new markets +13%) are all positive and bracket the total +8%, consistent with a broad-based recovery in September 2025.
Cumulative Jan-Sep 2025 totals and their YoY growth are internally consistent with the monthly September figures; same HKTB release.
p16 and p17 are the same ~23 million Jan-May 2026 preliminary figure from the same government speech; they are duplicate copies, not independent corroboration.

Full-year 2025 ~49.9m (p18) with +12% growth (p19) and Jan-May 2026 ~23m (p16) are consistent with continued strong 2026 momentum; the Jan-May 2026 run-rate (~4.6m/month) is above the 2025 monthly average (~4.16m/month), implying positive YoY growth into 2026.

Overnight arrivals, length of stay, per-capita spend and satisfaction are contextual quality metrics from the same HKTB work-plan reporting; they do not directly measure September 2026 total arrivals but support a stable-to-growing demand backdrop.

The best computed estimate for total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong (all source markets, all trip purposes, same-day and overnight) during September 2026, as the provisional HKTB figure, is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]).

The estimate anchors on the observed September 2025 provisional total of [[p1_value]] and applies a YoY growth factor of [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]). That factor is an assumption, not an observation: it reflects September 2025's growth and the stronger early-2026 run-rate, with moderating momentum assumed. The YoY factor already embeds September seasonality, so no separate seasonal adjustment is applied. Only one method was used ([[n_methods]]), carrying weight [[m1_weight]], so the combination is effectively that single method rather than an independent cross-check.

The main risk is the assumed growth factor: H2 2026 momentum, policy changes, or a Mainland travel shift could move arrivals well outside the range. The most useful missing evidence would be actual July–August 2026 monthly arrivals, which would pin down the current run-rate before September.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 2026 YoY growth factor for September total arrivals vs September 2025: [[a1_value]] ratio, range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]] (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of a sharp 2026 slowdown, new travel restrictions, or a major disruption in September 2026 that breaks the trend.

The best computed estimate for total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong (all source markets, all trip purposes, same-day and overnight) during September 2026, as the provisional HKTB figure, is 3,646,153 visitor (80% model-based interval 2,646,623 to 5,023,166 visitor).

The estimate anchors on the observed September 2025 provisional total of 3,292,197 visitor arrivals (person-trips) and applies a YoY growth factor of 1.1 (range 0.9895 to 1.237). That factor is an assumption, not an observation: it reflects September 2025's growth and the stronger early-2026 run-rate, with moderating momentum assumed. The YoY factor already embeds September seasonality, so no separate seasonal adjustment is applied. Only one method was used (1), carrying weight 100%, so the combination is effectively that single method rather than an independent cross-check.

The main risk is the assumed growth factor: H2 2026 momentum, policy changes, or a Mainland travel shift could move arrivals well outside the range. The most useful missing evidence would be actual July–August 2026 monthly arrivals, which would pin down the current run-rate before September.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 2026 YoY growth factor for September total arrivals vs September 2025: 1.1 ratio, range 0.9895 to 1.237 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Evidence of a sharp 2026 slowdown, new travel restrictions, or a major disruption in September 2026 that breaks the trend.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
